title: IIOBC files for consideration of charges in death of Everett Riley Edward Patrick
subtitle: In its investigation, the oversight agency "determined that reasonable grounds exist to believe that an officer may have committed offences in relation to the standard of care Mr. Patrick received."
article: The Independent Investigations Office of B.C. has announced that it has filed a report to the B.C. Prosecution Service for the consideration of charges in the death of Everett Riley Edward Patrick.

On April 12, 2020 at approximately 4:30 a.m., police responded to an alarm at E&I Sports on Third Avenue, which led to the arrest of Patrick hours later. He was taken to hospital before being cleared and brought to RCMP cells.

At 4 p.m. the same day, Patrick was found to be in "medical distress" in his cell and was returned to hospital via ambulance. When he arrived, he was "found to be suffering serious injury." He was pronounced dead on April 20.

Following his death in 2020, the civilian police oversight agency conducted an investigation and "determined that reasonable grounds exist to believe that an officer may have committed offences in relation to the standard of care Mr. Patrick received."

For charges to be approved, the B.C. Prosecution Service "must be satisfied that there is a substantial likelihood of conviction based on the evidence gathered by the IIO, and that prosecution be required in the public interest."
